_meta.source: Illustrative ORDC (Operating Reserve Demand Curve). ERCOT-style exponential function: penalty_price = exp(k × (1 - reserves/target)) when reserves < target.
_meta.description: Reserve penalty curve data points. Shows: low penalty at ~3,000 MW reserve (0.5% LOLP), rising exponentially, hitting VOLL at ~0 MW reserve.

parameters.formula: penalty = VOLL × exp(k × (1 - reserve_mw / target_reserve_mw)) when reserve < target

narrative.low_reserves: When available reserves exceed the target (3,000 MW), the ORDC penalty is near zero — demand relief is not critical.
narrative.tight_reserves: As reserves fall below target, the penalty rises exponentially. At 1,500 MW (binds ~5% of hours in a 10-year ERCOT backcast), penalty = ~$900/MWh.
narrative.scarcity: At 500 MW reserves (15–20% marginal risk), penalty ≈ $4,700/MWh. The ORDC becomes the marginal cost for the last MW of demand relief.
narrative.voll_clamp: Penalty clamps at VOLL ($5,000/MWh) at 0 MW reserves. This prevents the penalty from inverting load or inducing perverse incentives.

related_iso_odrc_parameters.CAISO: Different curve; uses RCPF (Resource Capacity Procurement Floor) mechanism post-2021. Similar exponential shape.
related_iso_odrc_parameters.PJM: Reliability Pricing Model (RPM) capacity market replaces day-ahead ORDC. Scarcity pricing in the RPM clearing.
related_iso_odrc_parameters.NYISO: ORDC in Energy and Ancillary Services Market (E-ASM). Embedded in the energy price; no separate reserve product.
